newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian 1996 non-CIS oil exports rise to 102 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russian 1996 non-CIS oil exports rise to 102 mln T.

text.p: Russian crude oil exports outside the Commonwealth of Independent States in 1996 rose 6.2 percent on 1995's level to 102.1 million tonnes (about 2.04 million barrels per day), the Fuel and Energy Ministry said on Thursday.

A ministry spokesman declined to provide absolute figures for 1995, but said that exports to the CIS, which does not include the Baltics, fell 25 percent in 1996 to 23.3 million tonnes (466,000 bpd) on the previous year's level.
Russia's total crude oil output in 1996 slipped two percent on 1995 to 293 million tonnes (around 5.86 million bpd), according to State Statistics Ministry figures published earlier this month.

Russia's main, Black Sea oil export outlet Novorossiisk boosted the amount of oil and oil products it handled in 1996 to 43.8 million tonnes, up over 40 percent from 30.7 million in 1995, the Transport Ministry said earlier this week.
Various government organisations compile energy export data and the numbers can differ.
